paper_title: A Controllable Examination for Long-Context Language Models
caption: The average performance of all models on Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness categories.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the average performance of multiple language models across three categories: Understanding, Reasoning, and Trustworthiness. The horizontal axis lists the model names – including “gpt-4o-2024-11-20”, “Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M”, and “Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407”, among others – and is labeled accordingly. The vertical axis represents percentage values, with a linear scale ranging from 0% to 100%, with tick marks every 20%. Each model’s performance is represented by a set of three horizontally stacked bars, one for each category. The “Understanding” bars are light blue, “Reasoning” bars are medium blue, and “Trustworthiness” bars are dark blue. For instance, “gpt-4o-2024-11-20” has a light blue “Understanding” bar extending to 98.0%, a medium blue “Reasoning” bar extending to 34.9%, and a dark blue “Trustworthiness” bar extending to 66.5%. Bars are sorted vertically in descending order based on the height of the “Understanding” portion; the tallest bar set is at the top and the shortest is at the bottom. Representative values for the shortest bar set are 2.4% for Understanding, 7.2% for Reasoning, and 0.0% for Trustworthiness, while the tallest bar set has 98.0% for Understanding, 34.9% for Reasoning, and 66.5% for Trustworthiness. No bars are visually emphasized beyond color differentiation for each category.
